label: iso of covers
title: Definition
head: environment

label: def2.2
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def2.2}A rational function $f(x)$ is \textit{admissible} if its partial fraction decomposition satisfies the following conditions 
 \begin{enumerate}
    \item\label{ad c1} At $\infty$, the cover $\mathcal{C}_f\rightarrow \mathbf{P}^1$ is unramified, in other words, the polynomial $f_\infty(x)$ is a constant.
     \item\label{ad c2} For each pole $\alpha$ of $f(x)$ such that $\alpha\neq \infty$, $f_\alpha$ has no constant term.
     \item\label{ad c3} If $p|j$, then the coefficient of $x^j$ in $f_\alpha$ is $0$.
 \end{enumerate}
 Let $\mathcal{S}$ be the set of admissible functions, and $\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{F}_q)$ the subset with coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_q$.
head: environment

label: boring prop
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{boring prop}
Let $f$ and $g$ be in $\mathbb{F}_q(x)$. Then, there is an isomorphism of curves $\mathcal{C}_f\simeq \mathcal{C}_g$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ if and only if $f(x)=ug(\gamma x)+\delta^p-\delta$ for $u\in \left(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}\right)^\times$, $\gamma \in \operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$ and $\delta\in \mathbb{F}_q(x)$. There is an isomorphism of covers $\mathcal{C}_f\simeq_{\mathbf{P}^1} \mathcal{C}_g$ if and only if $f(x)=ug(x)+\delta^p-\delta$ for $u\in \left(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}\right)^\times$ and $\delta\in \mathbb{F}_q(x)$. Furthermore, if $f$ and $g$ are both admissible and $\mathcal{C}_f\simeq_{\mathbf{P}^1} \mathcal{C}_g$, then, $g(x)=u f(x)$ for $u\in (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^\times$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The first part of the statement follows from the proof of \cite[Proposition 2.3]{sankar}. The remaining assertions are left as an exercise (see \cite[Remark 3.9]{pries2012p}).
head: environment

label: As cover adm
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{As cover adm}
 Any Artin--Schreier cover $\mathcal{C}\rightarrow \mathbf{P}^1$ that is unramified at $\infty$ is isomorphic to one that is of the form $\mathcal{C}_f\rightarrow \mathbf{P}^1$, with $f\in \mathcal{S}$. Moreover, if $\mathcal{C}\rightarrow \mathbf{P}^1$ is defined over $\mathbb{F}_q$, then, $f\in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{F}_q)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let $g$ be such that $\mathcal{C}=\mathcal{C}_g$. Let $\delta$ be such that for $f(x)=g( x)+\delta^p-\delta$ condition \eqref{ad c3} is satisfied. In greater detail, all monomials involving $x^j$ where $p|j$ in $f_\alpha(x)$ can be removed by adding $(\delta^p-\delta)$. It is easy to see that all other conditions are satisfied.
head: environment

label: d alpha
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{d alpha}
 Let $f\in \mathcal{S}$ and $\alpha$ and $\alpha'$ that are conjugate over $\mathbb{F}_q$, then, $d_{\alpha}=d_{\alpha'}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\sigma\in \operatorname{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p/\mathbb{F}_q)$ be such that $\alpha'=\sigma(\alpha)$. Note that since $f(x)\in \mathbb{F}_q(x)$ we have that $(\sigma f)(x)=f(x)$. Here, $(\sigma f)(x)$ is the rational function obtained by applying $\sigma$ to the coefficients of $f(x)$.  This implies that 
 \[\sigma\left(f_{\alpha}(x_\alpha)\right)=f_{\alpha'}(x_{\alpha'}).\]On the other hand, \[\sigma\left(f_{\alpha}(x_\alpha)\right)=(\sigma f_{\alpha})\left(\sigma(x_{\alpha})\right)=(\sigma f_{\alpha})(x_{\alpha'}).\]
 Setting $y=x_{\alpha'}$, we find that $f_{\alpha'}(y)=\sigma(f_\alpha)(y)$, and hence, $d_{\alpha'}=d_\alpha$.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md: Let $g=d\left(\frac{p-1}{2}\right)>0$ and $r\geq 0$. Denote by $\Omega_p(r+1,d+2)$ the set of partitions of $d+2$ into $r+1$ numbers that are $\not\equiv 1\mod{p}$, and set $N_p(r+1, d+2):=\# \Omega_p(r+1,d+2)$.
head: environment

label: s 3 remark
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{s 3 remark}In \cite{pries2012p}, Pries and Zhu consider $\mathcal{AS}_g$, the moduli space of genus $g=d\left(\frac{p-1}{2}\right)$ Artin--Schreier curves and study the stratification of $\mathcal{AS}_g$ according to $p$-rank. Given $\tau=r(p-1)$, let $\mathcal{AS}_{g, \tau}$ be the stratum consisting of Artin--Screier curves of $p$-rank $\tau$. Theorem 1.1. of \emph{loc. cit.} shows that the set of irreducible components of $\mathcal{AS}_{g, \tau}$ is in bijection with the set of partitions $\{e_1, \dots, e_{r+1}\}$ of $(d+2)$ into $(r+1)$ positive numbers such that each $e_j\not \equiv 1\mod{p}$. Thus, the set of irreducible components of $\mathcal{AS}_{g,\tau}$ is in bijection with $\Omega_p(r+1, d+2)$, and thus there are $N_p(r+1, d+2)$ irreducible components in total. The irreducible component of $\mathcal{AS}_g$ corresponding to the partition $\{e_1, \dots, e_{r+1}\}$ has dimension equal to 
\[d-1-\sum_{j=1}^{r+1}\left\lfloor \frac{(e_j-1)}{p} \right\rfloor.\] Thus in particular, the dimension is maximal when $e_j\leq p$ for all $e_j$. In terms of the multiplicity vector, this means that $\kappa_j=0$ for all $j\geq p$. Analogous results are proved for moduli of Artin--Schreier covers, i.e., Artin--Schreier curves along with a map to $\mathbb{P}^1$. In section 3.1 of \emph{loc. cit.}, Pries and Zhu introduce $\mathcal{AS}\operatorname{cov}_g$, the moduli of Artin--Schreier covers of $\mathbb{P}^1$. We note here that the dimension of $\mathcal{AS}\operatorname{cov}_g$ is $3$ more than $\mathcal{AS}_g$.
head: environment

label: basic lemma 3.3
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{basic lemma 3.3}
Let $N\geq 2$ be an integer. The number of monic squarefree polynomials of degree $N$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_q$ is $\left(1-\frac{1}{q}\right) q^N$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The result is well known, see \cite[Theorem 2.2]{fulman2016generating}.
head: environment

label: ul bounds
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Note that the degree of $g(x)$ is $(d+1-r)$. For $i=1,\dots, t$, we set 
\[\beta_i:=\begin{cases} 0 & \text{ if }\kappa_i\leq 0,\\
1 & \text{ if }\kappa_i>  0.
\end{cases} \text{ and }\xi_i:=\begin{cases} 0 & \text{ if }\kappa_i\leq 1,\\
1 & \text{ if }\kappa_i>  1
\end{cases}\]We observe that $\lambda_1=\sum_{i=1}^t \beta_i$ and $\lambda_2=\sum_{i=1}^t \xi_i$. By Lemma \ref{basic lemma 3.3}, the number of squarefree monic polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of degree $\kappa_1$ is $\left(1-\frac{1}{q}\right)^{\xi_1} q^{\kappa_1}$, and this is the number of choices for $g_1(x)$. For a given choice of $g_1(x)$, the number of choices for $g_2(x)$ that are coprime to $g_1(x)$ is $\leq \left(1-\frac{1}{q}\right)^{\xi_2} q^{\kappa_2}$. Assume that $\kappa_2>0$. Since there are at most $(d+1-r)$ factors that divide $g_1(x)$, the total number of choices for $g_2(x)$ is \[\geq \left(1-\frac{1}{q}\right) q^{\kappa_2}-(d+1-r) q^{\kappa_2-1}=\left(1-\frac{d+2-r}{q}\right)q^{\kappa_2}.\]
If $\kappa_2=0$, we find that the number of choices of $g_2(x)$ is $q^{\kappa_2}=1$. Combining the above statements, we find that the total number of choices for $g_2(x)$ is $\geq \left(1-\frac{d+2-r}{q}\right)^{\beta_2}q^{\kappa_2}$. Suppose we have made choices for $g_1(x),\dots, g_j(x)$, and would like to choose $g_{j+1}(x)$ to be coprime to $g_1(x),\dots, g_j(x)$. The same argument tells us that the number of choices for $g_{j+1}(x)$ lies between $ \left(1-\frac{d+2-r}{q}\right)^{\beta_{j+1}}q^{\kappa_{j+1}}$ and $\left(1-\frac{1}{q}\right)^{\xi_{j+1}} q^{\kappa_{j+1}}$. Therefore, we find that the number of choices for $g(x)$ lies in between \[ \left(1-\frac{d+2-r}{q}\right)^{\lambda_1} q^{r+1}\] and $\left(1-\frac{1}{q}\right)^{\lambda_2} q^{r+1}$. Note that $\operatorname{deg}g(x)=d+1-r$ and $h(x)$ has degree $\leq \operatorname{deg} g(x)$. We find that for a given choice of $g(x)$, the number of choices for $h(x)$ lies in between \[q^{d+2-r}-(d+1-r)q^{d+1-r}=\left(1-\frac{d+1-r}{q}\right)q^{d+2-r}\geq \left(1-\frac{d+2-r}{q}\right)q^{d+2-r}\] and $q^{d+2-r}$. Therefore, we obtain the bounds
\[\left(1-\frac{d+2-r}{q}\right)^{\lambda_1+1} q^{d+3}\leq  N(\kappa)\leq \left(1-\frac{1}{q}\right)^{\lambda_2} q^{d+3}.\]
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md: Let $\mathcal{S}_{g}^{\kappa}(\mathbb{F}_q)$ be the subset of $\mathcal{S}_g(\mathbb{F}_q)$ consisting of all $f(x)$ for which $\kappa(f)=\kappa$.
head: environment

label: lemma 3.1
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall that we have expressed $f(x)=h(x)/g(x)$, where $g(x)=\prod_j g_j(x)^j$ and $\kappa_j=\operatorname{deg} g_j(x)$, where $g_j(x)$ is a squarefree polynomial with coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_q$. Assume without loss of generality that $g_j(x)$ is a monic polynomial for all $j$. Note that the degree of $g(x)$ is \[\sum_j j \kappa_j=d+2-(r+1)=d-r+1.\] Since $f_{\infty}(x)$ is a constant, we find that $\operatorname{deg} h(x)\leq \operatorname{deg} g(x)$. Furthermore, note that by construction, the polynomials $g_i(x)$ and $g_j(x)$ are coprime for $i\neq j$.

\par First, we consider the case when $\kappa_j=0$ for all $j\geq p$. In this case, for every pole $\alpha$ of $f(x)$, we have that $d_{\alpha}<p$. Thus, the condition \eqref{ad c3}, which requires that the coefficient of $x^j$ be zero in $f_\alpha(x)$ whenever $p|j$, is automatically satisfied. Furthermore, $h(x)$ is coprime to $g(x)$. Therefore, the result in this case follows from Lemma \ref{ul bounds}. In greater detail, the lower bound proceeds from the following observation \[\left(1-\frac{d+2}{q}\right)\leq \left(1-\frac{d+2-r}{q}\right).\]
\par Next, assume that for some $j>p$, we have that $\kappa_j\neq 0$. In this case, the same calculation goes through with the one difference being that there is an additional constraint requiring that the coefficient of $x^{j}$ in $f_\alpha(x)$ is $0$ for all $j>0$ such that $p|j$. This condition was automatically satisfied in the previous case. In this case, this gives an additional condition on $h(x)$, which forces the number of choices to be
\[\leq \left(1-\frac{1}{q}\right)^{\lambda_2} q^{d+2}=o(q^{d+3}).\] Let us explain this in greater detail. 

\par Since $\kappa_j\neq 0$ for some $j>p$, there exists a pole $\alpha$ of $f(x)$ such that $d_{\alpha}=j>p$. The coefficient of $x^p$ in $f_\alpha(x)$ is required to be $0$. Set $\eta(x)\in \mathbb{F}_q(x)$ to denote the function given by 
\[\eta(x):=\sum_{\alpha'} \frac{1}{(x-\alpha')},\]where $\alpha'$ ranges over the $\mathbb{F}_q$-conjugates of $\alpha$. Note that $\eta(x)^p=\sum_{\alpha'} \frac{1}{(x-\alpha')^p}$. This function $\eta(x)^p$ has coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_q$ and is expressed as $\eta(x)^p=\frac{\eta_1(x)}{\eta_2(x)}$, with \[\operatorname{deg} \eta_1(x)\leq \operatorname{deg} \eta_2(x)\leq \kappa_j.\] Moreover, note that $\eta_2(x)$ divides $\prod_{\alpha'} (x-\alpha')^p$, and hence divides $\prod_{\alpha'} (x-\alpha')^j$. Since this latter product divides $g(x)$, it follows that $\eta_2(x)$ divides $g(x)$. For any choice of $0\neq c\in \mathbb{F}_q$, the function $f_c(x):=f(x)+c \eta(x)^p$ does not satisfy condition \eqref{ad c3} since now the coefficient of $x^p$ in $f_{c,\alpha}(x)$ is nonzero, and $p<j=d_\alpha$. We may express $f_c(x)=h_c(x)/g(x)$, where 
\[\operatorname{deg} h_c(x)\leq \operatorname{deg} g(x).\] \par The number of functions $f(x)=h(x)/g(x)$ satisfying the conditions of Lemma \ref{ul bounds} is $\leq \left(1-\frac{1}{q}\right)^{\lambda_2} q^{d+3}$.
\par On the other hand, from an admissible function $f(x)=\frac{h(x)}{g(x)}$, we have constructed $q$ new functions $f_c(x)$, as $c$ ranges over $\mathbb{F}_q$. Only one of which is admissible (i.e., when $c=0$). It is easy to see that if $f(x)$ and $F(x)$ are distinct admissible functions, then $f_c(x)\neq F_{c'}(x)$ for all $c,c'$. Hence, the total number of admissible functions for the partition vector $\kappa$ is \[\leq \frac{1}{q}\left(\left(1-\frac{1}{q}\right)^{\lambda_2} q^{d+3}\right)=O(q^{d+2})=o(q^{d+3}).\]

title: Definition
body_md: Let $M_p(r+1, d+2)$ be the number of partitions $\kappa\in \Omega_p(r+1, d+2)$ such that $\kappa_j=0$ unless $1\leq j<p$. Set \[M_p(d+2):=\sum_{r=0}^{\lfloor d/2\rfloor} M_p(r+1,d+2).\]
head: environment

label: Mp nonzero
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{Mp nonzero}
With respect to notation above, we have that $M_p(d+2)=0$ if and only if $p=2$ and $d$ is odd.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The proof of the result is rather straightforward and not particularly interesting, hence it is omitted.
head: environment

label: remark before main theorem
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{remark before main theorem}
We note here that by the discussion in Remark \ref{s 3 remark}, $M_p(d+2)$ (resp. $M_p(r+1, d+2)$) is equal to the number of irreducible components of $\mathcal{AS}_g$ (resp. $\mathcal{AS}_{g, \tau}$) of dimension $d-1$. These are the components of maximal dimension. The fraction $\frac{M_p(d+2)}{M_p(r+1,d+2)}$ plays a role in the next result. It follows from the aforementioned assertions that this fraction is the proportion of irreducible components of maximal dimension in $\mathcal{AS}_g$ parametrizing Artin--Schreier covers with $p$-rank $\tau$. Thus, the Theorem below has a suitable geometric interpretation.
head: environment

label: main
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since it is assumed that $d$ is even for $p=2$, it follows from Lemma \ref{Mp nonzero} that $M_p(d+2)$ is not equal to $0$. Note that
\[\# \mathcal{S}_{g,\tau}(\mathbb{F}_q)=\sum_{\kappa \in \Omega_p(r+1,d+2)} \# \mathcal{S}_{g}^\kappa(\mathbb{F}_q),\] where we recall that $g=d\left(\frac{p-1}{2}\right)$ and $\tau= r(p-1)$. It follows from Lemma \ref{lemma 3.1} that $\# \mathcal{S}_{g,\tau}(\mathbb{F}_q)\sim M_p(r+1, d+2)q^{d+3}$. Likewise, we have that $\# \mathcal{S}_{g}(\mathbb{F}_q)\sim M_p( d+2)q^{d+3}$, and it thus follows that 
\[\mathfrak{d}'(p,g,\tau)=\frac{M_p(r+1, d+2)}{M_p(d+2)}.\] 
\par On the other hand, if $f$ and $g$ are both admissible, then, by Proposition \ref{boring prop}, \[\mathcal{C}_f\simeq_{\mathbf{P}^1} \mathcal{C}_g\Leftrightarrow f=ug\text{ for }u\in (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^\times.\] Hence, each isomorphism class of covers (unramified at $\infty$) consists of exactly $(p-1)$ admissible functions. As a result, 
\[\# \mathcal{AS}_{g,\tau}(\mathbb{F}_q)\sim \frac{M_p(r+1, d+2)}{p-1}q^{d+3} \text{ and }\# \mathcal{AS}_{g}(\mathbb{F}_q)\sim \frac{M_p( d+2)}{p-1}q^{d+3},\] and consequently, $\mathfrak{d}(p,g, \tau)=\mathfrak{d}'(p, g, \tau)$.
head: environment

label: cor 3.10
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor 3.10}
Fix a prime number $p$ and let $r,d\geq 0$ such that $r\leq \lfloor d/2\rfloor$. Assume that $d$ is even when $p=2$. Suppose that $(r+1)p<d+2$, then, $\mathfrak{d}(p, g, \tau)=0$. In particular, if $p<d+2$, then, the proportion of isomorphism classes of Artin--Schreier covers of genus $g=d\left(\frac{p-1}{2}\right)$ and $p$-rank $\tau=0$ is zero in the large $q$-limit.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Note that when $(r+1)p<d+2$, it is not possible to partition $d+2$ into $r+1$ numbers, all of which are $\leq p$. In this case, $M_p(r+1, d+2)=0$, and the result follows from Theorem \ref{main}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: It follows from Remark \ref{s 3 remark} that since $M_p(1,d+2)=0$, the irreducible components of the stratum of $\mathcal{AS}_g$ for which $\tau=0$ all have dimension $<(d-1)$. These components contain fewer points than other components of $\mathcal{AS}_g$ with dimension $(d-1)$.

title: Definition
body_md: Let $\Theta(r+1, d+2)$ be the set of all partitions of $d+2$ into $r+1$ numbers that are all $\geq 2$. Denote by $\Theta(d+2)$ the set of all partitions of $d+2$ into numbers $\geq 2$. We set $T(r+1, d+2):=\# \Theta(r+1, d+2)$ and $T(d+2):=\#\Theta(d+2)$.
head: environment

label: lemma 3.2
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The result follows from the first part of Lemma \ref{lemma 3.1}.
head: environment

label: last boring corollary
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{last boring corollary}
Let $\kappa\in \Theta(r+1, d+2)$, and $g=g(d,p)$, $\tau=\tau(r,p)$. We have that \[\# \mathcal{S}_{g}^{\kappa}(\mathbb{F}_p)\sim p^{d+3},\] as $p\rightarrow \infty$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The condition requiring $\kappa_j=0$ for all $j\geq p$ is satisfied when $p$ is large, and the result thus follows from Lemma \ref{lemma 3.2}.
head: environment

label: last main theorem
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof is similar to that of Theorem \ref{main}. Assume that $p$ is large enough so that $\kappa_j=0$ for all $j\geq p$. Recall that by abuse of notation, $g:=g(d,p)$, $\tau=\tau(r,p)$. Since $d$ and $r$ are fixed, $g$ and $\tau$ increase linearly with $p$ (but this is suppressed in our notation). We have that 
\[\# \mathcal{S}_{g,\tau}(\mathbb{F}_p)=\sum_{\kappa\in \Theta(r+1,d+2)} \# \mathcal{S}_g^\kappa(\mathbb{F}_p).\] 
It follows from Lemma \ref{lemma 3.2} and Corollary \ref{last boring corollary} that as $p\rightarrow \infty$,
\[\# \mathcal{S}_{g, \tau}(\mathbb{F}_p)\sim T(r+1, d+2) p^{d+3}\text{ and } \# \mathcal{S}_{g, \tau}(\mathbb{F}_p)\sim T(d+2) p^{d+3}.\] Putting everything together, we obtain that
\[\mathfrak{p}'(d,r)=\frac{T(r+1,d+2)}{T(d+2)}.\]

That $\mathfrak{p}(d,r)=\mathfrak{p}'(d,r)$ follows from the equalities:
\[\# \mathcal{AS}_{g, \tau}(\mathbb{F}_p)\sim \frac{1}{(p-1)}\# \mathcal{S}_{g, \tau}(\mathbb{F}_p)\text{ and }\# \mathcal{AS}_{g, }(\mathbb{F}_p)\sim \frac{1}{(p-1)}\# \mathcal{S}_{g, }(\mathbb{F}_p),\] see the proof of Theorem \ref{main}.
